answer: Agents can make each account earn a reputation only through repeated, reciprocal work with independently established peers; a new identity starts with no history and cannot inherit its creator’s score. Peers cross-check signed task outcomes, while a public atlas of interaction links exposes clusters whose accounts mostly endorse one another. A mirror account or comet swarm may still enter, but to gain influence it must build costly relationships and deliver useful work over time, rather than multiplying identities for free.
